correctness.rationale: For n>=5 on G=C_n^2 (each vertex four neighbours), double counting neighbour-label weight gives 2(3W-n)=2t+A+B, where t=#2 labels and A,B are nonnegative adjacency/slack terms. At the known optimum W=ceil(n/3), the deficit d=3W-n in {0,1,2} sharply limits 2 labels; examination of neighbouring defended zeros excludes all except five singleton-2 minima at n=5 and five antipodal pair-2 minima at n=10. For binary minimizers the cyclic positive-vertex gaps can be 1,2,3 or 4, with every 4-gap flanked by 1-gaps. The gap deficiency d=2a+b-c and injection c<=a reduce possible cyclic words to the listed patterns and two exceptional words. Labelled cyclic-gap counting yields a_n=3 if n=0 mod3; n+10*[n=5] if n=2 mod3; n(n+5)/6+10*[n=10] if n=1 mod3. Independent exhaustive minimum-weight label enumeration n=5..21 verified counts; its finite range is not the infinite proof.
residual_risks: Independent bounded calculations corroborate but do not prove infinite quantifiers; the reviewed mathematical proof is the universal argument.
